purpose: Lane-free source-surface proposals before choosing HD-map traffic hypotheses.
path_conventions: Source paths are repository-relative; generated artifacts are job-relative; native extension paths are package-relative.
source_license: ODbL-1.0; database contents DBCL-1.0. Applies to derived evidence and figure.

figure.description: Unfiltered point-map XY context, input trajectory and observed candidate curves; source spans versus original input stations. Display sampling only; detection used the full saved point map.

warnings: Proposals follow spatially supported low surfaces, not semantic roads or lanes. A lower level can be wrong. Coverage gaps and search limits are not physical road edges; support spans are incomplete widths unless every section has two curb-like profiles. Check geometry, branches, obstacles, legal use and georeferencing. Repeated passes are separate proposals, not unique road length. Bin-centre edges have 0.5 m quantization; full-width interiors are not certified by three longitudinal support curves.

hd_compatibility_check.reason: Compatibility check only: corridor proposals leave complete width and traffic semantics unresolved. Reproduce the prior #214 review geometry with its unchanged explicit lane/width/traffic hypotheses; do not adopt a point-coverage span as road width.

warnings: Seed-road heights use the lowest 0.15 m layer within 0.75 m under the trajectory, with at least three occupied 0.2 m XY cells spanning a triangle of at least 0.01 m². Each cell contributes its lowest return; their median is used. Missing coherent support defers sections. Another level or wrong XY can still pass; compare both source estimators, actual boundaries and retained extent before selecting.
227 boundary vertices use the configured lane width rather than a detected feature.
196 curb-like height transitions lacked consistent road-side support or had excessive raised-surface height and were rejected; remaining candidates still require review.
145 inferred boundary vertices are positioned relative to detected outer boundaries; they remain width assumptions, not observed lane lines.
183 vertices selected a continuous candidate path. Rejected detections can become labelled width assumptions; source counts do not establish survey accuracy.
Some boundaries follow the end of point coverage; verify that they are road edges rather than scan gaps.
Draft map: verify lane counts, travel directions, junctions and boundary geometry before use.
